catalog_quote: Note that the personal pronouns are clitics and not affixes. This is evidenced by the fact that they do not change the stress as the suffixes do. That -an, -i, and -na are suffixes is shown by the fact that they cause the stress to be moved to the new penultimate syllable. So, tAnan becomes tanAnnii and jIllok becomes jillOkanni. The last -i in both verbs is the third person marker, which does not affect stress and is not therefore a suffix. [fn. 7, thesis p. 7:] Proclitics are clitics that attach to the front of the stems similarly to prefixes. The difference between clitics and affixes is not as immediately obvious with proclitics and prefixes as it is with enclitics and suffixes, where the suffixes affect the placement of stress and enclitics don't.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is penultimate: adding a true suffix (applicative -an, -i, possessive -na) shifts stress rightward onto the new penultimate syllable of stem+suffix (tánan -> tanán-ni-i, jíllok -> jillók-an-ni), whereas pronominal enclitics (e.g. 3rd-person -i, and the person clitics generally) lie outside the stress domain and leave stress where it was. Capital letters in the author's examples mark the stressed vowel.
new_statements.exceptions: Enclitic pronouns (and aspectual enclitics by implication) do not count for stress placement; proclitics ke- 'if/when', la- 'FUT' are written separately. No lexical exceptions discussed.
new_statements.domain_note: Domain is the grammatical word = stem plus suffixes, excluding enclitics; statement is made in passing as a clitic-vs-affix diagnostic in a morphosyntax thesis, not in a phonology chapter, and presupposes (rather than separately asserts) the default penultimate rule. Data from Baraka/Cakke area speakers (Imran Sandupa of Baraka, Dasa of Panyurak) collected 1987-1991 under UNHAS-SIL.
new_statements.identity_note: Source describes Duri proper (duri1242, ISO mvp), fieldwork 1987-1991 in Baraka and the Cakke-Kalosi area (consultants from Baraka and Panyurak), i.e. the Baraka / Cakke-Kalosi dialects; not the Benteng Alla dialect on the Toraja border. The Indonesian Pusat Bahasa volumes on the list of works to obtain treat 'bahasa Massenrempulu' as one language covering Duri, Enrekang (enre1234) and Maiwa (maiw1250), so any statement taken from them must be checked for which dialect it is based on.
